topic.title: Rates of Change in Polar Functions
topic.summary: When the graph of a polar function moves toward or away from the origin, relative extrema as points closest to or farthest from the origin, and the average rate of change of r with respect to θ.

lesson.title: Rates of Change in Polar Functions
lesson.summary: When the graph of a polar function moves toward or away from the origin, relative extrema as points closest to or farthest from the origin, and the average rate of change of r with respect to θ.
learningGoals: 3.15.A Describe characteristics of the graph of a polar function.
lesson.bigIdea: The distance from the origin is |r|, so whether a polar curve moves away from the origin depends on both the sign of r and whether r is increasing or decreasing. The average rate of change of r measures how fast the signed radius changes per radian.
lesson.context: Topic 3.14 drew polar graphs. This topic describes how they change, in the same language Unit 1 used for functions: increasing, decreasing, extrema, and average rates of change.

sections.title: 3.15.A · The sign of r and its direction of change decide the distance.
sections.conceptTitle: Distance from the origin and relative extrema

blocks.text: If a polar function, r = f(θ), is positive and increasing or negative and decreasing, then the distance between the point with polar coordinates (f(θ), θ) and the origin is increasing.
If a polar function, r = f(θ), is positive and decreasing or negative and increasing, then the distance between the point with polar coordinates (f(θ), θ) and the origin is decreasing.

blocks.caption: Is the point moving away from the origin?
r = 1 + 2 cos θ graphed with θ on the horizontal axis
blocks.alt: A cosine-shaped curve from r = 3 at θ = 0, decreasing through r = 0 at θ = 2π/3 to r = −1 at θ = π, then increasing back through 0 at 4π/3 to 3 at 2π.

blocks.text: Example: for r = 1 + 2 cos θ on 0 < θ < π, r is decreasing. On 0 < θ < 2π/3, r is positive, so the distance from the origin is decreasing. On 2π/3 < θ < π, r is negative, so the distance is increasing: the curve is tracing its inner loop outward.

For a polar function, r = f(θ), if the function changes from increasing to decreasing or decreasing to increasing on an interval, then the function has a relative extremum on the interval corresponding to a point relatively closest to or farthest from the origin.

blocks.title: Write it like the AP Exam
blocks.text: On 2π/3 < θ < π, the distance between the point (f(θ), θ) and the origin is increasing because f is negative and decreasing on that interval.

sections.takeaway: Same sign of r and its change: moving away. Opposite: moving closer.

sections.title: 3.15.A · Average rate of change of r with respect to θ.
sections.conceptTitle: Average rates of change in polar functions

blocks.text: The average rate of change of r with respect to θ over an interval of θ is the ratio of the change in the signed radius values to the change in θ over an interval of θ. Graphically, the average rate of change indicates the rate at which the signed radius is changing per radian.
The average rate of change of r with respect to θ over an interval of θ can be used to estimate values of the function within the interval.

Example: for r = 1 + 2 cos θ on 0 ≤ θ ≤ π/2, the average rate of change is (f(π/2) − f(0))/(π/2 − 0) = (1 − 3)/(π/2) = −4/π ≈ −1.273. On average, the signed radius decreases by about 1.273 units per radian on this interval.

Estimating with it: f(π/4) ≈ f(0) + (−4/π)(π/4) = 3 − 1 = 2. The actual value is 1 + 2 cos(π/4) = 1 + √2 ≈ 2.414, so the estimate is reasonable but not exact, because r does not change at a constant rate.

blocks.title: Units
blocks.text: The average rate of change of r with respect to θ is in units of radius per radian, the same kind of ratio as the average rates of change in Topic 1.2.

sections.takeaway: Δr/Δθ: change in signed radius per radian, useful for estimates inside the interval.

vocabulary.term: Average rate of change of r with respect to θ
vocabulary.definition: The average rate of change of r with respect to θ over an interval of θ is the ratio of the change in the signed radius values to the change in θ over an interval of θ. Graphically, the average rate of change indicates the rate at which the signed radius is changing per radian.

connections.title: Average rate of change
connections.body: Topic 1.2 defined the average rate of change of a function over an interval as the change in output over the change in input. For a polar function the output is the signed radius and the input is an angle.
connections.transferQuestion: Find the average rate of change of r = 2θ on 1 ≤ θ ≤ 3.

connections.transferQuestion: Which Unit 3 topic would you review to find the amplitude and midline from a graph?
connections.feedback: Topic 3.5, and Topic 3.7 for building a model from data.

glossary.definition: The polar coordinate system is based on a grid of circles centered at the origin and on lines through the origin. The positive x-axis is called the polar axis. Polar coordinates of a point are defined as an ordered pair, (r, θ). The value of θ is given by the measure of an angle in standard position whose terminal ray lies in a line that passes through the point, and r is the radial displacement of the point from the origin.
The graph of the function r = f(θ) in polar coordinates consists of input-output pairs of values where the input values are angle measures and the output values are radii.

glossary.term: Average rate of change of r with respect to θ
glossary.definition: The average rate of change of r with respect to θ over an interval of θ is the ratio of the change in the signed radius values to the change in θ over an interval of θ. Graphically, the average rate of change indicates the rate at which the signed radius is changing per radian.
